Internals npmatch and matchdb call

Source: R/for-npmatch.R
np_tokenize.Rd

Thin, exported wrappers around six internal helpers. npmatch's blocking, comparison and geography code, and matchdb's place keys, call these instead of reaching into this package's internals. Most users never call them.

Usage

np_tokenize(frame, token_col, stopwords, min_token_len, concat_adjacent)

np_doc_freq(row, token)

np_addr_key(street_keys, zip5 = NULL)

np_extract_unit(street, unit = NULL)

np_unit_id(unit)

np_state_abb(state)

Arguments

frame

A data frame holding token_col.

token_col

The column to tokenize.

stopwords

Tokens to drop (see np_stopwords()).

min_token_len

Shortest token kept.

concat_adjacent

Also index adjacent-token concatenations.

row, token

Parallel vectors: the row each token came from, and the token.

street_keys, zip5

Street keys and ZIP codes from np_normalize().

street

A free-text street or address line, as np_normalize() takes it in street.

unit

For np_extract_unit(), the canonical second address line, read only where street carries no unit; a bare value there is accepted ("300" gives "# 300"), since a dedicated unit column needs no designator to say what it is. For np_unit_id(), a suite as np_normalize() writes it in street_unit ("STE 300", "FL 2", "# 12").

state

State names or codes.

Value

np_tokenize(): a list of base and concatenated token tables. np_doc_freq(): a named numeric vector of row counts per token. np_addr_key(): a character vector of address keys. np_extract_unit(): a character vector of canonical units, NA where the address names none. np_unit_id(): a character vector of suite identifiers, NA where there is none. np_state_abb(): a character vector of two-letter codes, NA where none applies.

Details

  • np_tokenize() splits a column into tokens for the blocking index, as npmatch::np_ref_index() and npmatch::np_block() do.

  • np_doc_freq() counts, for each token, the rows it appears in.

  • np_addr_key() builds the address key np_addr_freq() counts on: the street key and ZIP, blank for a PO box.

  • np_extract_unit() reads the secondary unit out of one free-text address line, exactly as np_normalize() fills street_unit: "STE 300", "FL 2", "# 12", or NA where the line names no unit. This is the single-vector entry point onto the designator gate, for a caller holding a free-text line (a Form 990-PF address line 2, say) rather than a frame.

  • np_unit_id() reduces a suite as written to its identifier: the designator and separators are dropped, so "STE 300", "Suite 300" and "# 300" all give "300", and "STE D-2" gives "D2". This is the street_unit_id column np_normalize() adds, computed from street_unit.

    It is gated by the same designator pattern as np_extract_unit(), so a line that names no unit returns NA rather than a confident reduction of whatever was passed: "PO BOX 1367", "114 HIGH ST", "LAS VEGAS" and "400891" are all NA. A bare identifier with no designator ("300") is NA too, because a digit string on its own is as often a box number or a record counter as a door; pass a dedicated unit column as np_extract_unit()'s unit argument, where a bare value is accepted because the column itself says what it is.

  • np_state_abb() maps a state name or code to its two-letter code.

They are not part of the normalizer signature: each only calls functions that are (np_normalize_signature()), and adds nothing of its own.
